## What this guide is for

The dashboard downloads the ABS (Attention Bias Study) test-data CSV by logging
into the admin portal at `https://abs.la.utexas.edu` with a username and
password (`R/abs_login.R`). The login is unusual — the portal uses the
Livewire framework and sends malformed HTTP/2 headers — so the module has to
turn off SSL certificate checks and force HTTP/2. That works, but it makes the
failure modes a little unusual too.

Credentials come from two environment variables, both required:

- `ABS_USERNAME`
- `ABS_PASSWORD`

They live in `.Renviron` at the repo root and are loaded with
`source ./load-env.sh`.

**If you see** → **Cause** → **Fix**:

| If you see | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Not authenticated` | The tests page redirected back to the login page. The session expired, the password was rotated, or the credentials are wrong | Confirm both variables are set (`Sys.getenv("ABS_USERNAME")`), check the password was not rotated, then create a fresh session: `session <- abs_login()` |
| `Failed to load tests page` / redirect to `/admin/login` on every call | Same as above, but during the download step rather than the login step | Re-login and re-download in one session — `download_abs_csv()` requires the session object returned by `abs_login()` |
| SSL / connection errors (`certificate verify failed`, `malformed HTTP/2`, `connection reset`) | The ABS server serves broken HTTP/2 headers, so the module disables certificate verification (`ssl_verifypeer = 0`) and forces HTTP/2. Plain `httr2` code without those settings fails against this server | Do not "fix" the connection settings in custom code. Reuse `abs_login()` / `download_abs_csv()` as-is; they already carry the working settings |
| `make docker-test-auth` fails at the login step | The container could not read the credentials — it needs a `.Renviron` file at the repo root (mounted read-only), or the credentials inside it are wrong | Create `.Renviron` at the repo root with `ABS_USERNAME` and `ABS_PASSWORD`, then re-run `make docker-test-auth` |
| Login succeeds but the CSV has zero rows | The portal is up and authenticated, but the tests page has no data yet | Not a code problem — check the ABS portal in a browser with the same account |

## Testing the login the way the maintainers do

`make docker-test-auth` is the maintained end-to-end login check: it builds the
Docker image and, inside the container, logs in, downloads the CSV, and prints
how many rows came back. That is the single best command to run when you
suspect ABS credentials are the problem:

```{r docker-test-auth, eval=FALSE}
# From the repo root, in a terminal (requires Docker + a .Renviron file):
#   make docker-test-auth
#
# Expected happy-path output:
#   Login OK
#   Downloaded N rows
```

## Why the connection settings are weird (and why you should not touch them)

The ABS server sends headers that do not conform to the HTTP/2 specification.
A normal `httr2` request fails before it even reaches the login form. The
module works around this by:

- disabling certificate verification (`ssl_verifypeer = 0`,
  `ssl_verifyhost = 0`) so the malformed TLS handshake is tolerated, and
- forcing `http_version = 2`.

Both are confined to the module — nothing else in the dashboard disables TLS
checks. If you see TLS warnings in the log, they are expected and safe in this
one place.

## Still stuck?

- Read the module notes in `../docs/okf/modules/abs_login.md` — they document
  the redirect-detection and the exact environment-variable hygiene.
- If the failure only shows up in the daily build, see the CI troubleshooting
  vignette: the workflow needs `ABS_USERNAME` and `ABS_PASSWORD` set as
  repository secrets, and a rotated password will fail the same way locally
  and in CI.
